issues.failure_explanation: The right-hand side b_h(F,Psi_h) of the discrete source problem (3.5) is built from b_h^E, whose stabilization S_b^E is defined through the local degrees of freedom chi(.) (vertex values, Gauss–Lobatto values, moments). For general F=(g,f) in W = L^2 x L^2 (or even f in H^1), the vertex/edge values of f do not exist, so S_b^E((I-Pi^0)f, .) and hence b_h(F,Psi_h) are undefined. Consequently the discrete solution operators A_h: W -> V_h and T_h: L^2 -> L^2 used throughout (in particular in the claim ||T_h - T||_{L^2->L^2} -> 0 and ||A_h - A||_{V->V} -> 0, which drive the Babuska–Osborn theory) are not defined. The paper additionally defines A_h by a_h(A_h F,Psi_h) = b(F,Psi_h) (with b, not b_h) while asserting A_h F = U_h^F, the solution of (3.5) with b_h; with b, A_h is well defined on W but its eigenvalues are not those of the discrete eigenvalue problem (3.3), which uses b_h; with b_h, A_h is undefined outside V_h. The estimates (3.18) and I' in Lemma 3.4 explicitly manipulate S_b^E((I-Pi^0)f, .) for f in L^2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Introduce a well-defined extension of the discrete load (e.g., define the source term for f outside V_h in a computable way and prove consistency with (3.3) on V_h, or set up the Babuska–Osborn analysis on V_h/V with an operator that agrees with the eigenproblem's b_h on V_h), and reprove the operator-convergence statements with that definition; restate Lemmas 3.3–3.4 for the data class on which b_h is defined.
issues.overall_effect: Lemmas 3.3 and 3.4 (stated for arbitrary F in W), the operator-norm convergence claims, and hence Theorems 3.1 and 3.2, rest on discrete operators that are either undefined or inconsistent with the discrete eigenvalue problem (3.3); the L^2 spectral framework (rates (3.22), (3.23), (3.30), (3.31)) is unsupported as written.
issues.title: Discrete source problem / operators A_h, T_h ill-defined for data outside V_h (b_h needs degrees of freedom of f), and A_h defined inconsistently with b instead of b_h
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial redefinition and consistency argument (standard in the VEM eigenvalue literature) is needed; the expected results and rates plausibly survive, but no complete argument is present in the source.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since \({\bf \mathds{V}}_h \subset {\bf \mathds{V}}\), we also have the weak $\mathds{T}$-coercivity of $a_h(\cdot,\cdot)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds the diagonal terms from below with c_* and the cross term from above with c^* separately, and then needs an epsilon_4 with c^*/(gamma c_*) < epsilon_4 < c_*/c^*. Such an epsilon_4 exists only if (c^*/c_*)^2 < gamma, a condition on the stabilization equivalence constants that is neither assumed nor generally true (e.g., gamma close to 1 with c^*/c_* >= 2). The preceding justification 'Since V_h subset V' is also invalid because a_h is not the restriction of a. As written the proof does not establish (3.9) for all admissible gamma > 1 (and 'similarly' for gamma < 1).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply Cauchy–Schwarz and Young's inequality in the Hermitian positive semidefinite form a_h^E itself (a_h^E(phi,phi) - (2/gamma)Re a_h^E(psi,phi) + (1/gamma)a_h^E(psi,psi) >= (1-1/(gamma eps))a_h^E(phi,phi) + (1/gamma)(1-eps)a_h^E(psi,psi) for 1/gamma<eps<1) and only then invoke (3.7); this gives (3.9) with no condition on c^*/c_*.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 3.1 is unproved in the stated generality; it is used for discrete well-posedness and in the proof of Lemma 3.4.
issues.title: Proof of discrete T-coercivity (Lemma 3.1) requires an unstated condition (c^*/c_*)^2 < gamma
issues.why_classification: A short local reordering of standard inequalities repairs the proof; the statement and all downstream uses survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper asserts (3.11) with a constant independent of h, but the argument given (Gårding inequality (3.9) plus Fredholm alternative plus 'k^2 is not a discrete eigenvalue for small h') only yields existence/uniqueness for each fixed h; an h-uniform discrete inf-sup constant requires a separate Schatz-type argument (using T-coercivity, the compactness of the lower-order terms and an L^2 error bound). Moreover the claim that k^2 is not a discrete eigenvalue of (3.10) for small h is supported only by citing a paper on a different (Helmholtz anisotropic transmission) eigenvalue problem, not by a result for the VEM discretization (3.10) of (2.9).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a standard Schatz-type lemma: combine (3.9) with the duality L^2 estimate to show that for h sufficiently small a_h satisfies a discrete inf-sup condition on V_h with an h-independent constant, which yields both discrete uniqueness and (3.11).
issues.overall_effect: The uniform bound (3.11) is used for ||A_h||_V in (3.35) and implicitly throughout the a priori estimates; without it the constants in Lemmas 3.3–3.4 and Theorems 3.1–3.2 are not shown to be h-independent.
issues.title: Uniform-in-h discrete stability (3.11) not established; Fredholm alternative and cited eigenvalue convergence only give fixed-h well-posedness
issues.why_classification: The missing argument is standard and its ingredients (Lemma 3.1 and the duality estimate) are already in the paper; no claim or rate is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The term Re{a_h((w_pi,u_pi),(w_hat,w_hat)) - a((w_pi,u_pi),(w_hat,w_hat))} is declared to be 0. By the definition of b_h^E(n.,.) it equals -k^2 sum_E (n w_pi - Pi^0(n w_pi), w_hat - Pi^0 w_hat), which is nonzero whenever n is not piecewise polynomial; Lemma 3.2 itself is devoted to bounding exactly this term, and later in the same proof the analogous term with (w_hat,u_hat) is kept and estimated. Lemma 3.4 does not assume n piecewise constant, so the equality to zero is false and the term must be bounded (it is of order h^{1+min(l,s)}||w^f||_{1+min(l,s)}||w_hat||_1, hence harmless).

issues.failure_explanation: For the discrete operators one has b_h(A_h F,F*) = a_h(A_h F, A_h^* F*) = b_h(F, A_h^* F*), so b(T_h f, f*) and b(f, T_h^* f*) differ by [b - b_h](A_h F,F*) - [b - b_h](F, A_h^* F*); the asserted equality is therefore not exact and the subsequent decomposition I + II + III is derived from a false identity (a correct decomposition contains [b-b_h](F,A_h^*F*) instead of [b-b_h](A_hF,F*)). In addition, Babuška–Osborn Theorem 7.2 estimates |mu_j - (1/q) sum 1/(beta-lambda_{i,h})| for the eigenvalues mu = 1/(beta-lambda) of T, whereas (3.28) is written directly for the arithmetic mean of lambda_{i,h}; converting between the two introduces terms of order max_i|mu_j - mu_{i,h}|^2, which without an ascent assumption (absent from Theorem 3.1) are only O(eps^{2/alpha}) and need not be of order h^{2min(l,s)}. The spaces R(lambda_j), M(lambda_j) are also defined with eigenfunctions only, whereas the cited theorems concern generalized eigenspaces.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the first identity by the direct expansion b((A-A_h)F,F*) = a((A-A_h)F,(A^*-A_h^*)F*) + [b-b_h](F,A_h^*F*) + [a_h-a](A_hF,A_h^*F*) and estimate as before; state (3.23) for mu-means (or add the ascent hypothesis) and define M(lambda_j), R(lambda_j) as generalized eigenspaces.

issues.failure_explanation: The last inequality in (3.35) drops |lambda_{j,h}-lambda_j| on the grounds that it is 'small compared to' ||U_j - U_{j,h}||_V. The paper only has a priori upper bounds: |lambda_j - lambda_{j,h}| <~ h^{2min(l,s)} and ||U_j - U_{j,h}||_V <~ h^{min(l,s)}. No lower bound on the eigenfunction error is available, so |lambda_{j,h}-lambda_j| <= C||U_j - U_{j,h}||_V is not established (the eigenfunction error could be smaller than its a priori bound for particular eigenpairs/meshes). Hence (3.31), whose right-hand side involves the actual quantity ||U_j - U_{j,h}||_V rather than its a priori bound, is not proved as stated.
